title: Solve a monic quadratic equation by factorising

source_reference.notes: Original Edexcel 4MA1 Higher-style item for the Year 10 quadratics MVP. Edexcel pivot metadata applied.

student_prompt: Show your working and give both values of x.

error_category_mapping.diagnostic_sentence: The numbers 3 and 5 are right, but both factors must be negative because they add to -8 and multiply to +15.
You factorised correctly, but the command word is 'Solve'. After factorising, set each bracket equal to zero.
If x - 3 = 0, then x = 3. The sign changes when you solve the linear equation.

hint_ladder.title: What does Solve ask for?
hint_ladder.prompt: This is an equation set to zero. Think about what kind of values of x would make a product equal to zero. What is the connection between factorising and solving?

hint_ladder.title: Pick a starting move
hint_ladder.prompt: Try to rewrite the left side as a product of two brackets. The structure x^2 + (sum)x + (product) tells you what the brackets need to do.

hint_ladder.title: A common slip
hint_ladder.prompt: When the middle term is negative but the constant is positive, both factors carry the same sign. Check both conditions: product and sum.

hint_ladder.title: The general pattern
hint_ladder.prompt: For any x^2 + bx + c = 0 where you can factor it, rewrite as (x + p)(x + q) = 0, then use the zero-product principle to get x = -p or x = -q. Apply this pattern to your equation; do not copy an example.

common_errors: chooses correct numbers but wrong signs
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is choosing the signed factor pair before solving.

expected_solution_steps.action: set each bracket equal to zero
common_errors: does not use the zero-product property
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is moving from factorising to solving.

common_errors: gives only one value of x
expected_solution_steps.diagnostic_sentence: The stuck point is solving each bracket equation and giving both values.

mark_scheme_notes: Award 1 mark for correct factorisation, 1 mark for setting brackets equal to zero or equivalent method, 1 mark for both correct roots.
examiner_report_notes: Common errors expected: stopping after factorising, sign reversal in roots, giving one root only.
metacognition_prompt: Before you start, how is solving different from just factorising?
